gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the FOSSiBOT F2400 delivers from its AC outlets: techtest.org measured 1,512 Wh at a 100 W AC load (74% of the 2,048 Wh label), which is 15.1 hours at 100 W instead of the nameplate 20.5, and $0.442 per usable Wh at FOSSiBOT's own $669 price against $0.327 on the label.
standout_why: I could not open the cited rival pages: cheapestwh.com and outletpicks.com (both URL forms) failed with a certificate error in the fetch tool, and the direct download was blocked. The comparison therefore rests on their titles ("Cheapest … per Wh", "Cheapest 2,000–2,499Wh power stations") and on what ChatGPT drew from them: nameplate capacity, price, nameplate cost per Wh, warranty and weight. None of that includes a measured usable-Wh figure or a cost per warranty year. The Slickdeals ECO-WORTHY post, which I did open, states price and nameplate specs only, with no weight, cycle life or warranty. The score is 2 rather than 3 because the measured figure exists for the F2400 only, so it cannot rank the candidates against each other.
decides: It weakens ChatGPT's F2400 pick without replacing it. The F2400 is $669 at FOSSiBOT's US store today, so it is over budget there, and its AC-side energy is about 1.5 kWh, not 2 kWh. On warranty, which was ChatGPT's stated reason for the F2400, the AFERIY P210 costs $86.01 per warranty year (7 years, $602.10) against $133.80 for the F2400 (5 years, $669); the P210 is $2.10 over budget at AFERIY's store. The only price under $600 I could open was the ECO-WORTHY PS2400 at $516 through AliExpress on Slickdeals ($0.252/Wh nameplate), with warranty and cycle life not stated in that post.
